correctness.rationale: The repaired proof distinguishes words of lengths one, two and three: padding with 1 in the frozen argument did not preserve the two-nontrivial-idempotent norm identity. The corrected necessary discriminants for lengths one and two are 9 and (8β−1)²; at length three the predecessor quadratic gives the stated discriminant. The scalar cases in the lower bound now use D(0)=1 and D(1)=81. The predecessor plane is solvable in precisely the claimed cases: use a nondegenerate binary or larger complement for anisotropic vectors and the hyperbolic-plane decomposition for isotropic vectors; the residual ternary line has square class −Δ. For q≥5 the square-discriminant selection has at least three candidates against at most two bad norms; a single extra step handles the exceptional scalar coordinate. The q=3 split ternary bound is covered by the cited proposition and extends to higher dimensions by embedding each vector in a suitable ternary subspace. Independent full BFS of both ternary F3 algebras found 80 and 72 reachable elements and shortest-length widths 5 and 6. No change to the numerical theorem.
residual_risks: The independent enumeration checks only the two F3 ternary forms; the general statement rests on the proof.
